extracted.intended_audience: researchers, principal investigators, institution grants administrators, and applicants seeking NIDA/NIH grant funding
extracted.subtask_description: A summary of NIDA funding priorities, program-level funding mechanisms, and supplemental resources (FAQs, webinars, notices) that applicants should consult when preparing grant applications or requests for supplemental funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIDA Research Priorities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as the institute's thematic priorities for research funding; applicants should align proposals to these priorities to increase relevance and funding likelihood. (Page lists this as a top-level resource but does not list the individual priorities on this page.)

rubrics_metrics.name: NIDA Funding Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: A review of NIDA’s strategy for funding, based on programmatic priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how NIDA allocates funds across programmatic areas and reflects priorities applicants should consider when designing projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Special Interest (NOSI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of Special Interest (NOSI) - Formerly known as Drug Abuse Topics of Special/Continuing Interest (DAT)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOSI announce areas of special interest for which NIDA encourages grant applications; applicants should monitor NOSIs for targeted topics and special instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Advisory Council on Drug Abuse (NACDA) Approved Concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: National Advisory Council on Drug Abuse (NACDA) Approved Concepts – The purpose, scope, and objectives of approved concepts for potential funding opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NACDA-approved concepts indicate potential future funding announcements; used to anticipate forthcoming NOFOs and tailor proposals to emerging priority concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIDA Challenges Program
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDA Challenges Program – Crowd-sourced opportunities for providing solutions for particular goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenge competitions provide alternate, often rapid pathways for funding/recognition of solutions to specific problems; applicants should review challenge topics and rules for eligibility and submission format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for Research Training and Career Development
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for Research Training and Career Development – Grant funding opportunities for research training and career development at institutions across the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes training and career development FOAs (e.g., institutional T32, individual K awards); applicants should consult program-specific instructions and eligibility for trainee vs. early-career investigator awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Helping to End Addiction Long-term (HEAL) Initiative
rubrics_metrics.description: Helping to End Addiction Long-term (HEAL) Initiative – Congressional initiative to address the opioid overdose crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HEAL represents a major, targeted funding stream with specific priorities and RFAs; applicants should align proposals with HEAL goals and review HEAL-specific FOAs and FAQs.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIDA International Program
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDA International Program – International research collaboration opportunities on drug abuse and addiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports cross-national collaborations; applicants should review eligibility, partner requirements, and FOA specifics for international components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources for Grants & Contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: See NIDA’s Resources for Grants & Contracts to learn more about applying for a grant and the pre-approval and approval process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central resource for procedural guidance (application steps, submission, pre-approval, award administration); essential for first-time applicants and institutional administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Supplements for Grants & Cooperative Agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative Supplements for Grants & Cooperative Agreements – Additional funding to an active NIDA grant or cooperative agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism to request extra funds for specific, often time-limited activities; applicants must have an active parent award and follow the supplement NOFO/notice instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental Information for NOFOs (webinars, FAQs, pre-application presentations)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists numerous specific supplemental items (e.g., Pre-Application Information Virtual Presentation for TranSINDA NOFOs RFA-DA-25-037 and RFA-DA-25-038; FAQs for Avenir Award Program RFAs; Pre-Application Webinar for PAR-21-183 Developing Digital Therapeutics; FAQs about standard THC unit notice, HEAL supplements, biospecimen access programs, RFA-specific FAQs). Applicants should consult these supplemental materials (webinars, FAQs, notices of intent, pre-application presentations) for NOFO-specific clarifications, submission tips, timelines, and eligibility details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where NIH FOAs are posted (procedural change)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning in fiscal year 2026, NIH will no longer post notices of funding opportunities in the NIH Guide. To find NIH notices of funding opportunities please explore the NIH Grant Opportunities search tool which links to grants.gov, NIH’s single official source for grant and cooperative agreement funding opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must use the NIH Grant Opportunities search tool and grants.gov as the authoritative sources for FOAs after FY2025; note NOT-OD-25-143 for the official announcement of this change.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIDA Funding App retirement notice
rubrics_metrics.description: As of October 2025, the NIDA Funding App has been retired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not rely on the NIDA Funding App for listings; use the NIH and grants.gov tools noted above.
